title: Paris
extract:
The Paris is a Tenno bow that focuses on  Puncture damage. Simple to use, it is one of the first Primary Weapons new Tenno obtain from the Awakening quest, alongside the Braton.
This weapon can be sold for  7,500.

This weapon deals primarily  Puncture damage.

Acquisition
The Paris's blueprint can be purchased from the Market.

Notes
Enemies will notice missed arrows but arrows that hit are silent.
Arrows have a large amount of momentum, allowing players to pin enemies to walls. However, a dead body will not lose its momentum if it hits a closed door, so the body will fly through it as soon as the door opens.

Incarnon Genesis

Upon completion of The Duviri Paradox and Angels of the Zariman, and unlocking The Steel Path, players can earn  Paris Incarnon Genesis from The Circuit's Steel Path to place on their Paris with the help of Cavalero in the Chrysalith. This Incarnon Genesis form grants it evolutions to a transformation and newfound strength.
Purchased from Cavalero for  120, complete with the resources used in its installation. This purchase can only be made once.

Installing the Paris Incarnon Genesis requires 20  Pathos Clamps, 60  Rune Marrow, and 60  Silphsela.
When installed, the first Evolution tier is unlocked. Each challenge additionally grants 5,000 affinity to the weapon, affected by Affinity Boosters.

Overview
Incarnon Form is charged by filling the Incarnon Transmutation gauge that appears under the reticle by achieving weakpoint hits and then pressing the Alternate Fire button. 4 weakpoints hits will completely fill the gauge. A full gauge is not required to activate Incarnon Form.
Charges do not generate on the backpacks of most MOA variants, or vulnerability spots generated by  Sonar or  Detect Vulnerability in places other than actual weakpoints.
Weakpoints on corpses or Invulnerable targets do not build charges.
Individual Multishot bullets can build charges.
Mode switching is not instantaneous and has an animation equal to the weapon's reload speed.
Swapping to and from Incarnon Form will fully reload the normal form's magazine.
Instead of drawing ammunition from its reserves, the Paris's Incarnon Form uses a separate "magazine" with each charge producing 5 rounds to a maximum of 20. Once all ammunition is expended, the Paris reverts to its normal form.
Incarnon Form's magazine is not affected by mods.
Incarnon Form is not affected by Ammo Efficiency (such as  Energized Munitions).
Charges and Incarnon Form persists through all activities, such as holstering, bleedout, or being disarmed. However, charges and Incarnon Form are removed upon death.

Evolutions

Tips
As one of the player's choices for their starting Primary weapon, the Paris will likely be their first introduction to Bows, and weapons with a charge mechanic in general, allowing them to learn how to both use and mod weapons like it.
The primary fire input must be held for the weapon's listed charge time in order for shots to deal maximum damage and velocity. Arrows loosed before a full charge will have reduced velocity, and use the "Quick Shot" stats shows in the Arsenal rather than the "Charge Shot" stats.
Not every shot needs to be fully charged, however; quick shots can be used to quickly kill groups of weak enemies, such as Grineer Lancers and Butchers. Charged shots can instead be saved for more durable foes, such as Eximus.
On weapons that charge before firing, modifying the fire rate stat will increase or decrease the weapon's charge rate accordingly, something further augmented by a special mechanic with Bows where fire rate mods have their effects doubled on them. For instance, Speed Trigger will allow the Paris to pull back arrows near-instantly, while Critical Delay will make it take much longer.
The Paris's arrows have physical travel time, necessitating the user leads targets both horizontally and vertically outside of close-range engagements in order to compensate. Terminal Velocity can be installed on the Paris to compensate, ideally in its exilus mod slot.
Maintaining a charge ahead of a combat encounter can make engaging a group of enemies easier. Most charge weapons, such as the Paris, can continue charging and holding a charge while sprinting, sliding, aim gliding, and using most prompts involving the Use key. Hard landings from falling too far will also usually not interrupt a charge.
Charging can be cancelled without releasing the arrow using the reload button (Press the reload button while holding fire).
Using elevators and opening co-op doors does not cancel the charge, however hacking consoles and opening lockers will. So will picking up a holdable item that forces you to switch to your Secondary weapon, such as power cells in Excavation.
The Paris relies more on high damage-per-shot over volume of fire, unlike the Braton. Misses are more punishing, while accurate hits are more rewarding. While the player should always aim for headshots with most ranged weapons, the player especially should with the Paris to ensure each shot does the maximum possible damage.
This makes the Paris especially ammo efficient relative to the size of its ammo reserve capacity (the standard 72 arrows of most Bows). The player will thus rarely run out of ammo for the weapon unless it's especially under-modded for the current mission. If more ammo is needed regardless, a rank 1  Arrow Mutation is usually more than enough to keep ammo topped off.
Weapons like the Paris are normally capable of hitting more than one enemy per shot in some way; in its case, its charged shots have 2 meters of punch through. Positioning yourself to hit multiple enemies in a line, or using abilities such as Mag's Pull to clump enemies together, can allow you to damage or kill more than one enemy per arrow, compensating for the weapon's low rate of fire.
This punch through also allows the Paris's arrows to be shot through thin walls and still hit an enemy, or through physical shields such as a Shield Lancer's shield.
The Paris's damage being weighted primarily towards Puncture means it will deal more damage towards Corpus enemies especially, though its high damage relative to when the weapon is obtained means it will generally perform well against any faction. Its precision nature makes it well-suited to bypassing Corpus enemies' shield gating by taking them out with single headshots.
Magnetic or Toxin damage can be added to the weapon to further increase its lethality against Corpus enemies, though this is generally unnecessary until the player has progressed a few planets into the star chart, as Corpus are relatively frail even without faction damage bonuses (or Toxin's ability to bypass shields).
The weapon's high critical chance but low status chance make it well-suited to mods that increase the former (and with it, critical damage). A max-rank copy of Point Strike alone will increase the Paris's critical chance to 75%, causing every three arrows to be critical for every one that isn't, on average.
The Paris's Puncture weighting means that it will often apply Puncture status to enemies when it successfully procs a status effect on hit. Puncture's status effect both decreases the victim's damage output and increases how likely they are to take critical hits by a flat value, up to 80% and 25% respectively at the maximum count of 5 stacks. This can further increase the Paris's critical output, but only if its low status chance allows the effect to proc in the first place.
The Paris, being a Bow, is considered "Silent" when firing; enemies will not react to the sound of arrows being loosed. This makes the weapon ideal for the greater use of stealth in early-game Warframe compared to other Primary weapons; Exterminate missions can be completed without the player taking any damage, and Spy missions pose a much lesser risk of data vault alarms being triggered.
While other early-game Primary weapons can have Hush installed to become silent, most lack the Paris's affinity for killing in a single shot. Enemies killed by Bows, such as the Paris, also tend to cause the victim's corpse to be impaled by the arrow and fly along with it until it hits a wall, displacing it and reducing the likelihood other enemy patrols will see it.

Bugs
After charging an arrow and firing it while zooming, the next arrow you fire will not be drawn from the quiver, and instead the Paris and your hand will jerk very slightly. The next shot will show the reloading animation correctly.

Trivia
Paris is most likely named for Paris of Troy in Homer's Iliad, who was a skilled archer and the one to have killed Achilles by firing an arrow into his heel.
The Paris is the only bow that does not have a tension spring, as the arrow is held in place and launched by magnetic induction rather than physical force.
The Paris is modeled after a decurve bow.
